speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you're experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance. To help me understand what's happening, have you noticed if these symptoms worsen when you quickly turn your head or stand up? Also, have you experienced any recent head trauma or changes in your hearing?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for those details; the relief from diphenhydramine suggests a vestibular origin, but the constant spinning is unusual. Given your recent increased garlic intake, have you noticed any changes in your vision, such as double vision or halos, or any numbness in your hands? Also, have you had any difficulty speaking or swallowing recently?
